\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p03-vaught-two-cardinal}{cited=Vaught1965CardinalsFarApart}{Vaught's two-cardinal theorem}
Let \(T\) be a countable first-order theory in a language containing a unary
predicate \(U\). If \(T\) has a model \(M\) with
\(|M|>|U^M|\ge\aleph_0\), then \(T\) has a model \(N\) with
\(|N|=\aleph_1\) and \(|U^N|=\aleph_0\). The countability of the language and
the distinguished unary predicate are part of the statement; the theorem does
not prescribe arbitrary pairs of infinite cardinals.
\end{hbtheorem}
text:
\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p03-vaught-two-cardinal}{cited=MorleyVaught1962}{Vaught's two-cardinal theorem}
Let \(T\) be a countable first-order theory in a language containing a unary
predicate \(U\). If \(T\) has a model \(M\) with
\(|M|>|U^M|\ge\aleph_0\), that is, a two-cardinal model for \(U\) in the
sense of \cref{def:p03-w03-p03-029-kappa-lambda-model}, then \(T\) has a
model \(N\) with \(|N|=\aleph_1\) and \(|U^N|=\aleph_0\). The countability of
the language and the distinguished unary predicate are part of the
statement. The conclusion is the single pair \((\aleph_1,\aleph_0)\); the
theorem does not prescribe arbitrary pairs of infinite cardinals.
\end{hbtheorem}

\noindent\emph{Method sketch.}
Expand the theory so that a long indiscernible sequence lies outside the
distinguished predicate while Skolem closure over countably many parameters
keeps the predicate part countable. Compactness supplies finite pieces, and an
Ehrenfeucht--Mostowski construction stretches the sequence to length
\(\aleph_1\). This records the mechanism but not every Skolemization and
indiscernibility lemma; the theorem's proof status remains the cited one.
text:
\noindent\emph{Method sketch and scope.}
The theorem is Theorem~6.2 of Morley and Vaught, stated there for relational
systems with countably many relation symbols
\cite[pp.~54--55]{MorleyVaught1962}; the passage to languages with function
and constant symbols is \cref{thm:p03-w03-p03-029-theory-form}. The proof
uses countable homogeneous models. The L\"owenheim--Skolem theorem gives a
proper elementary substructure with the same predicate; this is replaced by a
countable homogeneous pair of isomorphic models with a common predicate, and
an elementary chain of length \(\omega_1\) of copies with that fixed
predicate has the required union (\cref{def:p03-w03-p03-029-mv-method}).
The theorem is not any of the following transfer theorems. The downward
L\"owenheim--Skolem theorem keeps the predicate and lowers a two-cardinal
model only to a pair \((\lambda^+,\lambda)\)
(\cref{thm:p03-w03-p03-029-gap-one}). The upward L\"owenheim--Skolem theorem
enlarges the universe without control of the predicate. Vaught's theorem for
cardinals far apart needs a gap of at least \(\beth_\omega\) above the
predicate and reaches every pair \((\lambda',\mu')\) with \(\lambda'>\mu'\);
the indiscernible-sequence method belongs to it. Chang's transfer moves
\((\lambda^+,\lambda)\) up to \((\mu^+,\mu)\) under \(\mu=\mu^{<\mu}\)
\cite[p.~4, items~(G) and~(H)]{Shelah2004PairAlephN}. The comparison is
\cref{def:p03-w03-p03-029-not-conflate}. The theorem's proof status remains
the cited one.
